functions.name: InitializeCharacterTables
functions.comment:
Initializes character lookup tables and locale-specific character mappings for the current code page.

Algorithm:
1. Retrieve code page information using GetCPInfo() with the global code page identifier
2. If code page info valid, initialize base character table with identity mapping (0-255)
3. Set character at index 0 to space character for proper handling
4. Process multi-byte character lead byte ranges to mark them as spaces in character table
5. Call FUN_10021c9e to generate character type flags for the character set
6. Generate uppercase mappings using LocaleMapStringWithConversion with flag 0x100
7. Generate lowercase mappings using LocaleMapStringWithConversion with flag 0x200
8. Iterate through all 256 characters and populate global character tables:
   - If character type flag & 0x1 (uppercase): set flag 0x10, use lowercase mapping
   - If character type flag & 0x2 (lowercase): set flag 0x20, use uppercase mapping
   - Otherwise: clear character mapping entry
9. If code page info invalid, fall back to ASCII-only mappings:
   - For A-Z (0x41-0x5A): set flag 0x10, add 0x20 for lowercase
   - For a-z (0x61-0x7A): set flag 0x20, subtract 0x20 for uppercase
   - For all other characters: clear mapping entry

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void - Function operates on global character tables DAT_1003cac0 and DAT_1003cbc0

Special Cases:
- Character 0 is always mapped to space (0x20) for proper null character handling
- Lead bytes in multi-byte character sets are marked as spaces to prevent misinterpretation
- Falls back to basic ASCII case mapping if code page information unavailable

Magic Numbers:
0x100 - LCMAP_UPPERCASE flag for LocaleMapStringWithConversion
0x200 - LCMAP_LOWERCASE flag for LocaleMapStringWithConversion  
0x10 - Character flag indicating uppercase letter
0x20 - Character flag indicating lowercase letter
0x1 - Character type flag for uppercase character
0x2 - Character type flag for lowercase character
0x41-0x5A - ASCII range for uppercase letters A-Z
0x61-0x7A - ASCII range for lowercase letters a-z

Error Handling:
- GetCPInfo failure triggers fallback to ASCII-only character mappings
- Lead byte processing handles ranges safely with bounds checking
- Character table initialization ensures all 256 entries are properly set

Structure Layout:
_cpinfo structure (18 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type    Description
0x0     4     MaxCharSize   UINT    Maximum character size in bytes
0x4     12    DefaultChar   BYTE[2] Default replacement character 
0x6     12    LeadByte      BYTE[12] Lead byte ranges for MBCS

functions.name: OptimizedMemoryMove
functions.signature: void * OptimizedMemoryMove(void * pDestination, void * pSource, uint dwByteCount)
functions.comment:
Optimized memory move implementation with overlap detection and alignment optimization.

Algorithm:
1. Check for overlapping memory regions (source and destination ranges overlap)
2. If overlapping regions detected, copy backwards from end to start to avoid corruption
3. If no overlap, copy forwards from start to end for better cache performance
4. For both directions, optimize copying using 4-byte aligned transfers when possible
5. Handle misaligned data by copying individual bytes first to reach alignment
6. Perform bulk 4-byte transfers in optimized loop (unroll threshold of 8 iterations)
7. Copy remaining bytes (0-3) using individual byte transfers

Parameters:
pDestination - Destination memory buffer to copy data to
pSource - Source memory buffer to copy data from  
dwByteCount - Number of bytes to copy between buffers

Returns:
void * - Returns original destination pointer (pDestination) for function chaining

Special Cases:
Zero byte count - Returns immediately without any memory operations
Misaligned pointers - Falls back to byte-by-byte copying with alignment handling
Large transfers - Uses optimized 4-byte transfers with loop unrolling for performance

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x4 (4) - Alignment boundary and 4-byte transfer size
0x3 (3) - Alignment mask to check 4-byte boundary alignment  
0x7 (7) - Loop unrolling threshold for optimized bulk transfer

Error Handling:
No explicit error checking - assumes valid memory regions and non-null pointers
Overlap detection prevents memory corruption during overlapping copies
Alignment optimization ensures optimal performance on x86 architecture

functions.name: AllocateStackSpace
functions.comment:
Dynamically allocates stack space with page probing to ensure proper memory commitment.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize stack pointer to current position plus 8 bytes (beyond return address and saved ECX)
2. Check if requested allocation size exceeds one page (0x1000 bytes)
3. If multi-page allocation needed, enter probing loop:
   - Subtract one page (0x1000 bytes) from stack pointer
   - Subtract one page from remaining allocation size
   - Touch memory at stack pointer to trigger page commitment
   - Repeat until remaining size is less than one page
4. Subtract final remaining bytes from stack pointer
5. Touch memory at final stack position to commit last page
6. Update ESP register to new stack pointer position
7. Restore original ECX and return address from saved stack frame
8. Return to caller with stack space allocated and committed

Parameters:
dwStackSize (uint) - Number of bytes to allocate on stack

Returns:
void - No return value, modifies stack pointer directly

Special Cases:
- Single page allocations (≤ 0xFFF bytes) skip the probing loop
- Memory touches use TEST instruction to trigger page faults for uncommitted pages
- Stack grows downward, so allocation decreases stack pointer
- Function preserves ECX register across call

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1000 (4096) - Windows page size for stack probing
0xFFF (4095) - Maximum single-page allocation without probing

Error Handling:
- No explicit error handling - relies on Windows page fault mechanism
- Invalid memory access triggers system page fault handler
- Stack overflow protection handled by system guard pages

functions.name: CloseStreamByIndex
functions.comment:
Closes and invalidates a stream descriptor by index, clearing its file handle.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream index against global stream count boundary
2. Calculate stream descriptor using bucket indexing: bucket = index >> 5, offset = index & 0x1F
3. Check if stream is active (nPosition & 1) and not already invalidated (pBase != 0xFFFFFFFF)
4. If global exit flag is set, clear standard handles for stdin(0)/stdout(1)/stderr(2)
5. Mark stream descriptor as invalidated by setting pBase = 0xFFFFFFFF
6. Return success (0) if stream was valid and closed
7. Set thread error context (errno=9, GetLastError=0) and return failure (-1) for invalid streams

Parameters:
nStreamIndex (uint): Zero-based index into global stream descriptor array

Returns:
int: 0 on successful stream closure, -1 if stream index invalid or already closed

Special Cases:
Stream indices 0, 1, 2 correspond to stdin, stdout, stderr standard handles
Global exit flag (g_dwExitFlag2) triggers standard handle cleanup via SetStdHandle

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1F (31): Mask for within-bucket offset (32 descriptors per bucket)
0x5: Right shift for bucket calculation (divide by 32)
0xFFFFFFFF: Sentinel value indicating invalidated stream descriptor
0xFFFFFFF6 (-10): STD_INPUT_HANDLE constant
0xFFFFFFF5 (-11): STD_OUTPUT_HANDLE constant  
0xFFFFFFF4 (-12): STD_ERROR_HANDLE constant
0x9: EBADF errno code (Bad file descriptor)

Structure Layout:
StreamIO (36 bytes total)
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type    | Description
0x00   | 4    | pBase      | void *  | File handle or buffer base pointer
0x04   | 4    | nPosition  | uint    | Current position/flags (bit 0 = active)
0x08   | 28   | [fields]   | varies  | Additional stream metadata

Array Indexing:
g_apStreamDescriptors uses bucket-based indexing for memory efficiency:
- bucket = nStreamIndex >> 5 (divide by 32)
- offset = nStreamIndex & 0x1F (modulo 32) 
- Each bucket contains 32 StreamIO descriptors (32 * 36 = 1152 bytes)
- Total address = g_apStreamDescriptors[bucket] + (offset * 36)

functions.name: GetOsFileHandle
functions.comment:
Retrieves the base data pointer for a valid stream descriptor from the global stream table.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream index against global stream count (g_dwStreamCount)
2. Calculate bucket index using right shift: nStreamIndex >> 5 (divide by 32)
3. Calculate element index within bucket: nStreamIndex & 0x1f (modulo 32) 
4. Access stream descriptor using two-level indexing: g_apStreamDescriptors[bucket][element]
5. Check stream validity flag in nPosition field (bit 0 must be set)
6. Return pBase pointer if stream is valid and active
7. Set thread context error code 9 (invalid stream) if validation fails
8. Clear thread context error code to 0
9. Return 0xffffffff (-1) to indicate error

Parameters:
nStreamIndex (int): Zero-based index into global stream descriptor table

Returns:
void *: Base data pointer for valid stream, 0xffffffff (-1) on error

Special Cases:
Index >= g_dwStreamCount: Invalid index, return error
Stream nPosition bit 0 clear: Stream not active/valid, return error
Valid stream: Return actual pBase pointer from StreamIO structure

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1f (31): Bit mask for modulo 32 operation (element index within bucket)
0x5 (5): Right shift count for divide by 32 operation (bucket calculation) 
0x9 (9): Thread context error code for invalid stream access
0xffffffff (-1): Error return value indicating invalid stream

Structure Layout:
StreamIO (36 bytes total):
Offset  Size  Field Name   Type      Description
0x00    4     pBase        void*     Pointer to stream data buffer
0x04    4     nPosition    uint      Stream position with validity flag in bit 0
0x08    28    [other]      [varies]  Additional stream management fields

Indexing Scheme:
Two-level bucket system for stream descriptor storage:
- g_apStreamDescriptors[bucket_index][element_index]
- bucket_index = nStreamIndex >> 5 (supports up to 32 * bucket_count streams)
- element_index = nStreamIndex & 0x1f (0-31 within each bucket)
- Each StreamIO structure is 36 bytes (9 DWORDs)

functions.name: AcquireStreamCriticalSection
functions.comment:
Acquires exclusive access to a stream by entering its critical section.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate bucket index by shifting stream ID right by 5 bits (divide by 32)
2. Calculate slot index by masking stream ID with 0x1F (modulo 32)
3. Retrieve stream descriptor pointer from global stream descriptor table
4. Check if critical section is initialized (pCurrent != NULL)
5. If not initialized, acquire global initialization lock (index 0x11)
6. Double-check initialization state under lock
7. If still uninitialized, initialize critical section and mark as initialized
8. Release global initialization lock
9. Enter the stream-specific critical section for exclusive access

Parameters:
dwStreamId (uint) - Stream identifier used to locate the corresponding stream descriptor

Returns:
void - Function does not return a value

Special Cases:
- Double-checked locking pattern prevents race conditions during initialization
- Global lock index 0x11 serializes critical section initialization across all threads
- Stream descriptors organized in buckets of 32 streams each for efficient lookup

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1F (31) - Bitmask for modulo 32 operation to get slot index within bucket
0x11 (17) - Global critical section index for stream initialization synchronization
5 - Right shift amount to divide stream ID by 32 for bucket calculation

Structure Layout:
StreamIO structure (36 bytes):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
   +8  |  4   | pCurrent   | void*| Initialization marker (NULL=uninitialized)
   +12 |  24  | dwFlags    | CRITICAL_SECTION | Windows critical section object

Algorithm Verification:
Step 1: dwSlotIndex = dwStreamId & 0x1F (MOV EAX,param; AND EAX,0x1f)
Step 2: bucket = dwStreamId >> 5 (MOV ECX,param; SAR ECX,0x5)  
Step 3: pStreamDescriptor = g_apStreamDescriptors[bucket] (MOV ESI,[ECX*4+g_apStreamDescriptors])
Step 4: Check pStreamDescriptor[dwSlotIndex].pCurrent == NULL (CMP [ESI+EDI+0x8],0x0)
Step 5: AcquireCriticalSectionByIndex(0x11) if uninitialized
Step 6: InitializeCriticalSection(&pStreamDescriptor[dwSlotIndex].dwFlags)
Step 7: EnterCriticalSection(&pStreamDescriptor[dwSlotIndex].dwFlags)

functions.name: ReleaseCriticalSectionForStreamSlot
functions.comment:
Unlocks the critical section for a stream descriptor using bucket-based indexing.

Algorithm:
1. Extract bucket index from stream index using right shift by 5 bits (divide by 32)
2. Extract offset within bucket using bitwise AND with 0x1F (modulo 32)
3. Calculate descriptor address using bucket array and 36-byte stride
4. Access dwFlags field at offset +12 within StreamIO structure
5. Call LeaveCriticalSection to release the critical section lock

Parameters:
dwStreamIndex (uint) - Zero-based stream identifier used for bucket/offset calculation

Returns:
void - No return value, unlocks critical section synchronously

Special Cases:
Stream indexing uses bucket system: bucket = index >> 5, offset = index & 0x1F
Each bucket contains 32 StreamIO descriptors at 36-byte stride
Critical section is embedded at offset +12 (dwFlags) within StreamIO structure

Structure Layout:
StreamIO structure (36 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name    Type                Description
0x00    ?     ?             ?                   Unknown fields
0x0C    24    dwFlags       CRITICAL_SECTION    Synchronization lock

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1F (31) - Mask for extracting offset within 32-entry bucket
0x5 (5) - Right shift count for bucket calculation (log2(32))
0xC (12) - Offset to dwFlags/CRITICAL_SECTION within StreamIO
0x24 (36) - Size of StreamIO structure for stride calculation

functions.name: ValidateAndProcessEntity
functions.comment:
Validates game entity and processes resource if flag conditions are met.

Algorithm:
1. Call entity validation function (FUN_6ff31731) with entity pointer
2. If validation fails (returns non-zero), return error code -1
3. Check entity flags byte at offset 0xd for resource processing flag (0x40)
4. If resource flag not set, return success (0)
5. If resource flag is set, call resource processing function (FUN_6ff3193d)
6. Return negated boolean result from resource processing

Parameters:
pEntity (int *) - Pointer to game entity structure being validated/processed

Returns:
-1 - Entity validation failed
 0 - Success (entity valid, no resource processing needed OR processing succeeded)
<0 - Resource processing failed (returns -1 if processing function returns non-zero)

Special Cases:
Flag 0x40 at offset 0xd controls resource processing branch
Resource handle at entity[4] (offset 0x10) passed to processing function

Structure Layout:
Offset  Size  Field Name           Type    Description
0x00    4     field_0x0           uint    Unknown field
0x04    4     field_0x4           uint    Unknown field  
0x08    4     field_0x8           uint    Unknown field
0x0c    1     field_0xc           byte    Unknown field
0x0d    1     bFlags              byte    Entity flags (bit 0x40 = resource processing)
0x0e    2     field_0xe           ushort  Unknown field

functions.name: FlushOutputBuffer
functions.comment:
Flushes pending write data from output buffer to underlying stream handle

Algorithm:
1. Check if stream is in write mode (flags & 0x3 == 0x2) and buffered output enabled (flags & 0x108)
2. Calculate pending bytes as current_pointer - base_pointer
3. If pending bytes > 0, call WriteToValidatedStream with file handle, base pointer, and byte count
4. If write successful (bytes written equals pending bytes):
   - Clear dirty flag (flags & 0xfffffffd) if buffering flag (0x80) is set
5. If write failed, set error flag (flags | 0x20) and return -1
6. Reset buffer state: set count to 0 and current pointer to base pointer
7. Return 0 on success, -1 on write failure

Parameters:
pFileStream (FILE*): Pointer to FILE structure containing buffer state and flags

Returns:
0 on success (buffer flushed successfully or no pending data)
-1 on write failure (WriteToValidatedStream returned different byte count)

Special Cases:
Stream not in write mode or buffering disabled - no operation performed, returns 0

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x2 - Write mode flag (bits 1-0 = 10 binary)
0x3 - Mode mask for extracting write/read mode bits
0x108 - Buffered output enabled flags (0x100 | 0x8)
0x80 - Buffer dirty flag indicating pending writes
0x20 - Error flag set when write operations fail
0xfffffffd - Mask to clear dirty flag (inverts 0x2)
0xffffffff - Error return value (-1)

Structure Layout:
FILE structure (_iobuf) accessed at these offsets:
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
   0   |  4   | _ptr       | char* | Current position in buffer
   4   |  4   | _cnt       | int   | Characters remaining in buffer
   8   |  4   | _base      | char* | Base address of buffer
  12   |  4   | _flag      | uint  | File status flags
  16   |  4   | _file      | int   | File handle/descriptor

Flag Bits:
0x01 - Read mode
0x02 - Write mode / Dirty flag
0x08 - Line buffering enabled
0x20 - Error condition occurred
0x80 - Buffer requires flushing
0x100 - Full buffering enabled

functions.name: ProcessLockContextEntities
functions.comment:
Iterates through lock context table and processes entities based on validation mode

Algorithm:
1. Acquire global critical section (index 2) for thread-safe access
2. Initialize loop counters and result variables to zero
3. Iterate through all entries in global lock context table (g_ppLockContextTable)
4. For each valid lock context entry, check if entity flags contain active bits (0x83)
5. Acquire conditional critical section for the specific lock context
6. Re-verify entity flags after acquiring lock (double-checked locking pattern)
7. Process entity based on mode parameter:
   - Mode 1 (Count Mode): Count successful validations, increment success counter
   - Mode 0 (Fail-Fast Mode): Return error (-1) on first validation failure if bit 0x02 set
8. Release conditional critical section for the lock context
9. Continue to next lock context entry until all processed
10. Release global critical section (index 2)
11. Return appropriate result based on processing mode

Parameters:
nProcessMode (int): Processing mode selector
  - 0 = Fail-fast validation mode (returns -1 on first failure)
  - 1 = Count mode (returns count of successful validations)

Returns:
Mode 0: Returns 0 on success, -1 if any entity with flag 0x02 fails validation
Mode 1: Returns count of successfully validated entities (>= 0)

Special Cases:
- Empty lock context table (g_nLockContextCount <= 0): Returns 0
- NULL lock context entries are skipped silently
- Entities without active flags (0x83) are skipped
- Mode 0 only processes entities with flag 0x02 set

Flag Bits Reference:
0x01 - Entity active/allocated flag
0x02 - Entity requires validation flag (mode 0 processing)
0x80 - Entity processing ready flag
0x83 - Combined active flags mask (0x01 | 0x02 | 0x80)

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x83 (131) - Active entity flags mask for initial check
0x02 (2) - Validation required flag for mode 0 processing
2 - Global critical section index for lock context table access
-1 - Validation failure/error return code

Error Handling:
- ValidateAndProcessEntity() returns -1 on validation failure
- Mode 0: First validation failure terminates processing with -1 result
- Mode 1: Validation failures are ignored, only successful validations counted
- Critical sections ensure thread-safe access to shared lock context table

Structure Layout:
LockContext structure (accessed at offset 0x0C for flags):
Offset | Size | Field Name | Type | Description
0x00   | ?    | data       | ?    | Context data array
0x0C   | 4    | flags      | uint | Entity status and control flags

functions.name: LocaleMapStringWithConversion
functions.signature: int LocaleMapStringWithConversion(uint dwLcid, uint dwMapFlags, char * lpszSrcStr, int nSrcLen, char * lpszDestStr, int nDestLen, uint dwCodePage, int nFlags)
functions.comment:
Performs locale-aware string mapping with automatic character encoding conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Set up structured exception handling (SEH) frame
2. Initialize Unicode support detection if not already done
   a. Test LCMapStringW with empty string to detect Unicode support
   b. If Unicode fails, test LCMapStringA for ANSI support
   c. Set global flag (1=Unicode, 2=ANSI) based on results
3. Validate source string length using FUN_1001fb97 if positive length
4. Branch based on detected encoding support:
   - If ANSI mode (flag=2): Call LCMapStringA directly and return result
   - If Unicode mode (flag=1): Perform conversion sequence
5. Unicode conversion sequence:
   a. Use default code page if dwCodePage is 0
   b. Calculate required wide character buffer size with MultiByteToWideChar
   c. Allocate stack space for wide character conversion buffer
   d. Convert source string from multibyte to wide character
   e. Get required output buffer size with LCMapStringW
   f. If LCMAP_SORTKEY flag (0x400) is set:
      - Return required size if output buffer is NULL
      - Validate output buffer size and perform mapping directly
   g. If normal mapping:
      - Allocate second stack buffer for wide character output
      - Perform LCMapStringW mapping to wide character buffer
      - Convert result back to multibyte using WideCharToMultiByte
6. Clean up SEH frame and return result

Parameters:
dwLcid (uint): Locale identifier for mapping operation
dwMapFlags (uint): Mapping flags controlling case conversion and sorting
lpszSrcStr (char *): Source string in multibyte encoding
nSrcLen (int): Length of source string (-1 for null-terminated)
lpszDestStr (char *): Output buffer for mapped string
nDestLen (int): Size of output buffer in characters
dwCodePage (uint): Code page for character conversion (0 = default)
nFlags (int): Additional conversion flags for MultiByteToWideChar

Returns:
Number of characters written to output buffer on success
0 on failure (insufficient buffer, conversion error, or unsupported operation)

Special Cases:
If lpszDestStr is NULL, returns required buffer size
LCMAP_SORTKEY flag (0x400) returns sort key instead of mapped string
Automatic fallback from Unicode to ANSI if Unicode APIs unavailable

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x100 - LCMAP_LOWERCASE flag for case conversion test
0x400 - LCMAP_SORTKEY flag for sort key generation
0x220 - WC_NO_BEST_FIT_CHARS | WC_COMPOSITECHECK flags
0x1003ca54 - Global Unicode support flag (1=Unicode, 2=ANSI)
0x1003c8e4 - Default code page storage

Error Handling:
Returns 0 for all error conditions including:
- Unsupported locale or mapping flags
- Insufficient output buffer space
- Character conversion failures
- Stack allocation failures

functions.name: CalculateStringLengthWithLimit
functions.comment:
Calculate the length of a null-terminated string with maximum limit.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize current pointer to start of string and remaining counter to max length
2. If max length is zero, skip to step 5
3. Loop while remaining length > 0:
   a. Decrement remaining length counter
   b. Check if current character is null terminator, if so break loop
   c. Advance current pointer to next character
4. Continue loop until null terminator found or max length reached
5. Check if null terminator was found:
   a. If found: return actual string length (current pointer - original pointer)
   b. If not found: return max length parameter (string exceeds limit)

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated string buffer to measure
nMaxLength (int): Maximum number of characters to examine before stopping

Returns:
int: Actual string length if null terminator found within limit
     Maximum length parameter if string exceeds specified limit
     Zero if maximum length parameter is zero

Special Cases:
- Returns 0 if nMaxLength is 0 (no characters to examine)
- Returns nMaxLength if no null terminator found within limit
- Handles empty string (immediate null terminator) correctly by returning 0

functions.name: ThreadSafeFileClose
functions.comment:
Thread-safe file close with critical section protection and flag management.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize return value to 0xffffffff (failure/invalid handle code)
2. Check if FILE._flag has 0x40 bit set (close-in-progress or error flag)
3. If flag 0x40 is clear: perform thread-safe close operation
   a. Acquire critical section lock for file pointer address
   b. Call __fclose_lk to perform actual close operation
   c. Store close result in dwResult
   d. Release critical section lock for file pointer address
4. If flag 0x40 is set: clear all flags to reset file state
5. Return close operation result or 0xffffffff

Parameters:
pFile (FILE*): Pointer to file stream to close. Must not be NULL.

Returns:
0 on successful close, -1 (0xffffffff) on error or if close was already in progress.
Returns 0xffffffff immediately if file has close-in-progress flag set.

Special Cases:
Magic number 0x40: FILE._flag bit indicating close-in-progress or error state
Magic number 0xffffffff: Standard error return value for file operations

Flag Bits:
FILE._flag & 0x40: Close-in-progress or error state flag
  0x40 set: File close already initiated or in error state
  0x40 clear: File available for normal close operation

functions.name: __fclose_lk
functions.comment:
Standard C Runtime library function - closes a file stream with thread-safe locking.
Library Function: Visual Studio 2003 Release (__fclose_lk maintains standard naming)

Algorithm:
1. Initialize return value to -1 (error state)
2. Check if file stream is valid by testing flags (0x83 = readable|writable|opened)
3. If valid stream:
   a. Flush any pending output data to underlying file
   b. Free internal stream buffers using __freebuf
   c. Close underlying file descriptor via FUN_6ff31a7d
   d. If close fails, set return value to -1
   e. If temporary filename exists, deallocate it and clear pointer
4. Clear all file stream flags to mark as closed
5. Return result code (0 = success, -1 = error)

Parameters:
pFile - Pointer to FILE structure representing the stream to close

Returns:
0 on successful closure of all resources
-1 if any cleanup operation fails (flush, buffer free, or file descriptor close)

Special Cases:
If FILE._flag & 0x83 == 0, stream is already closed - skip cleanup, only clear flags
If FILE._tmpfname is NULL, no temporary file to deallocate
Function always clears _flag to 0 regardless of cleanup success/failure

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x83 (131) - FILE flag mask for stream validity (readable|writable|opened bits)
0x0C (12)  - Offset to FILE._flag field in FILE structure  
0x10 (16)  - Offset to FILE._file field (underlying file descriptor)
0x1C (28)  - Offset to FILE._tmpfname field (temporary filename pointer)

Error Handling:
FlushOutputBuffer failure: Continues with cleanup, final result depends on file close
FUN_6ff31a7d (file close) failure: Sets nResult to -1, continues with temp file cleanup
DeallocateMemory failure: Not checked, assumes successful deallocation

functions.name: FlushStreamBuffer
functions.comment:
Flush the file buffer for a specified stream to ensure all pending write operations are committed to disk.

Algorithm:
1. Validate stream index against global stream count (g_dwStreamCount)
2. Check if stream is active by testing bit 0x1 in StreamIO.nPosition field
3. Acquire critical section lock for thread-safe access to stream descriptor
4. Re-validate stream active state (double-check pattern)
5. Get file handle from stream using GetStreamBasePointer()
6. Call Windows FlushFileBuffers() API to commit pending writes
7. Handle flush result - capture error code if flush failed
8. Set thread context error fields based on operation result
9. Release critical section lock regardless of success/failure
10. Return success (0) or failure (0xFFFFFFFF)

Parameters:

functions.comment:

1. Check immediate termination flag (DAT_1003c944) - if set, terminate process immediately using TerminateProcess
2. Set termination active flag (DAT_1003c940 = 1) to indicate termination is in progress
3. Store defer exit flag in global state (DAT_1003c93c) as byte value from nDeferExit parameter

   a. Check if cleanup function pointer array exists (DAT_1003cdf0 != NULL)
   b. Calculate start position at end of array (DAT_1003cdec - 4) for LIFO iteration
   c. Iterate backwards through function pointer array calling each non-null cleanup function
   d. Call RunConstructorArray for address range 0x1002a014 to 0x1002a018
5. Always call RunConstructorArray for address range 0x1002a01c to 0x1002a020 regardless of cleanup mode
6. Check defer exit flag - if nDeferExit is non-zero, return without exiting process
7. Set final termination flag (DAT_1003c944 = 1) and call ExitProcess with specified exit code

functions.name: RunConstructorArray

   a. Load the function pointer value into EAX
   b. Test if pointer is non-null (TEST EAX,EAX) 
   c. Skip null pointers (JZ to increment)
   d. Call the function pointer (CALL EAX) with no parameters
3. Advance to next function pointer (ADD ESI,0x4)
4. Continue until reaching end pointer (CMP ESI,[ESP+0xc])
5. Return when all valid function pointers have been executed

Parameters:

- ppfnEnd (void * *): Pointer to end of function pointer array (exclusive)

Returns:
- void: No return value

Special Cases:

- Empty array (ppfnStart == ppfnEnd) exits immediately
- No parameter validation - assumes valid array bounds

- Relies on caller to provide valid array bounds
- Function calls are made with no error checking

functions.name: FreeMemoryBlockWithLinkedListCleanup
functions.comment:
Frees a memory block and performs associated linked list cleanup and bit mask management.

Algorithm:
1. Extract memory descriptor base address from pDescriptor[4]
2. Get original block size from memory header at (dwBlockAddress - 4)
3. Calculate slot index using (dwBlockAddress - pDescriptor[3]) >> 15
4. Get previous block info from (dwBlockAddress - 8)
5. Adjust block size by subtracting 1 from original size
6. Calculate free list head pointer using slot index * 516 + 324 + descriptor base
7. Read current block info from adjusted position
8. If current block is not marked as allocated (bit 0 clear):
   a. Extract block index from bits 4-31, clamp to maximum 63
   b. If linked list pointers are equal (empty list):
      - Clear corresponding bit in bit mask arrays at offsets 0x44/0xC4
      - Decrement reference counter at descriptor base + block index + 4
      - If counter reaches 0, clear bit in main descriptor bit mask
   c. Update linked list forward/backward pointers
   d. Add current block size to adjusted size
9. Calculate new block index from adjusted size, clamp to maximum 63
10. If previous block exists and is not allocated:
   a. Extract previous block index, clamp to maximum 63
   b. Add previous block size to total adjusted size
   c. Recalculate new block index, clamp to maximum 63
   d. If indices differ, perform same bit mask and linked list operations as step 8
   e. Update linked list pointers for previous block
11. If conditions require re-linking or previous block was allocated:
   a. Link current block into free list at new block index
   b. Update forward and backward pointers in linked list
   c. If linking into empty list:
      - Increment reference counter
      - Set corresponding bit in bit mask arrays
      - If counter was 0, set bit in main descriptor bit mask
12. Store final adjusted size in block header and size field
13. Decrement free list head reference count
14. If reference count reaches 0 and global descriptor exists:
   a. Free virtual memory using VirtualFree with 0x8000 size and 0x4000 type
   b. Update global bit masks and counters
   c. If all bits cleared (0xFFFFFFFF), perform full cleanup:
      - Free entire virtual memory region
      - Free heap memory for descriptor
      - Compact descriptor array using OptimizedMemoryMove
      - Update global counters and pointers
      - Adjust function parameter pointer if necessary

Parameters:
pDescriptor (MemoryDescriptor *): Pointer to memory descriptor containing virtual memory base, heap memory base, and management data
dwBlockAddress (uint): Address within allocated memory block to be freed

Returns:
void

Special Cases:
- Block index clamped to maximum 63 (0x3F) to prevent array bounds overflow
- Bit operations split between two 32-bit masks for indices 0-31 and 32-63
- Empty linked lists trigger bit mask updates and reference counting
- Global cleanup only occurs when all blocks in a descriptor are freed

0x204: Size of free list management structure (516 bytes)
0x144: Offset to free list head array within descriptor (324 bytes)
0x44: Offset to lower 32-bit mask array (68 bytes)
0xC4: Offset to upper 32-bit mask array (196 bytes)
0x43: Offset to reference counter (67 bytes)
0x20: Boundary between lower and upper bit mask arrays

functions.name: AllocateMemoryDescriptorBlock
functions.comment:
Allocates memory block from descriptor-based allocator with size-class free lists

Algorithm:
1. Align requested size to 16-byte boundary and calculate size class index
2. Generate bitmasks for free block tracking based on size class (splits at 32-bit boundary)
3. Search descriptor array for available descriptor with matching free blocks
4. If no descriptor found, search from beginning for any available descriptor
5. If still no descriptor, search for descriptor with zero reserved field
6. If no descriptor available, call allocation expansion function (FUN_1001db6e)
7. If expansion fails, initialize new descriptor with FUN_1001dc1f
8. Locate appropriate free list and find block of suitable size
9. Calculate bit position for free block tracking within size class
10. Remove block from free list by unlinking (doubly-linked list operations)
11. If block larger than needed, split block and reinsert remainder into appropriate size class
12. Update bit tracking arrays and reference counts for block allocation
13. Set block headers with size information for boundary tag system
14. Update global state if this was the last block in descriptor
15. Return pointer to allocated memory (block pointer + 4 for header skip)

Parameters:
- nRequestedSize (uint): Size in bytes to allocate, will be aligned to 16-byte boundary

Returns:
- void*: Pointer to allocated memory block, or NULL if allocation fails

Special Cases:
- Sizes are rounded up to next 16-byte boundary (add 0x17, mask with 0xfffffff0)
- Free blocks tracked using dual bitmask system (low 32 bits, high 32 bits)
- Size classes use bit positions 0-63 for different allocation sizes
- Block splitting occurs when allocated block significantly larger than request
- Boundary tag system maintains size at block start and end for coalescing

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x17 (23): Alignment padding for 16-byte boundaries
- 0xfffffff0: Mask for 16-byte alignment
- 0x20 (32): Bit boundary for high/low bitmask split
- 0x3f (63): Maximum size class index
- 0x81 (129): Stride for free list array access (129 dwords per size class)
- 0x51 (81): Base offset for free list pointers in allocator data
- 0x31 (49): Offset to high bitmask in allocator data
- 0x11 (17): Offset to low bitmask in allocator data
- 0x80000000: High bit mask for bit manipulation operations

0x04   | 4    | pVirtualMemory| void*             | Pointer to virtual memory
0x08   | 4    | dwReserved1   | uint              | Reserved field, 0=available
0x0C   | 4    | dwFlags       | uint              | Descriptor flags/status

- Returns NULL if descriptor initialization (FUN_1001dc1f) returns -1
- Gracefully handles empty free lists by searching alternate size classes
- Validates descriptor boundaries before proceeding with allocation

3. Update g_dwBufferElementSize by adding 0x10 and store new array pointer in g_pDescriptorArray
4. Calculate pointer to next available descriptor (g_pDescriptorArray + g_nDescriptorCount)
5. Allocate 0x41c4 bytes of heap memory using HeapAlloc with HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag (0x8)
6. Store heap allocation pointer in descriptor dwReserved3 field
7. Allocate 1MB (0x100000) of virtual memory using VirtualAlloc with MEM_RESERVE flag (0x2000)
8. Store virtual allocation pointer in descriptor dwReserved2 field
9. Initialize descriptor fields: dwReserved1 = 0xffffffff, clear pVirtualMemory and pHeapMemory
10. Increment global descriptor count (g_nDescriptorCount)
11. Set first DWORD of heap memory to 0xffffffff as initialization marker
12. Return pointer to pVirtualMemory field of the new descriptor

Parameters:
None

Returns:
void * - Pointer to pVirtualMemory field of allocated descriptor on success
NULL - If descriptor array reallocation fails, heap allocation fails, or virtual memory allocation fails

Special Cases:
If heap allocation succeeds but virtual memory allocation fails, the heap memory is freed to prevent leaks before returning NULL

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x10 (16) - Descriptor array growth increment
0x41c4 (16836) - Size of heap allocation per descriptor
0x100000 (1048576) - Virtual memory allocation size (1MB)
0x2000 (8192) - MEM_RESERVE flag for VirtualAlloc
0x8 (8) - HEAP_ZERO_MEMORY flag for HeapAlloc
0xffffffff (-1) - Initialization value for dwReserved1 and heap memory marker

0x00   | 4    | pVirtualMemory  | void *  | Pointer to virtual memory allocation
0x04   | 4    | pHeapMemory     | void *  | Pointer to heap memory allocation
0x08   | 4    | dwReserved1     | uint    | Status/flags field, initialized to 0xffffffff

functions.name: AllocateMemorySlot
functions.comment:
Allocates a memory slot in the memory descriptor system and initializes linked list structures.

Algorithm:
1. Extract base offset from memory descriptor (offset 0x10)
2. Find next available slot by counting leading set bits in allocation mask (offset 0x8)
3. Calculate descriptor offset: slot_index * 0x204 + 0x144 + base_offset
4. Initialize 64 linked list node pairs (0x3f iterations) with self-referencing pointers
5. Calculate memory base address: slot_index * 0x8000 + base_address (offset 0xc)
6. Allocate 32KB (0x8000 bytes) of virtual memory with VirtualAlloc
7. If allocation fails, return -1
8. Initialize memory block as doubly-linked list with 1024-byte (0x400) stride
9. Set up forward and backward pointers for each node in the allocated block
10. Link descriptor to allocated memory at specific offsets (0x1fc, 0x200)
11. Clear slot status flag at base_offset + 0x44 + slot_index * 4
12. Set slot allocation flag at base_offset + 0xc4 + slot_index * 4
13. Increment allocation counter at base_offset + 0x43
14. If counter wraps to 0, set overflow flag (bit 0) in descriptor flags (offset 0x4)
15. Clear allocated bit in allocation mask using bit manipulation

Parameters:
pMemoryDescriptor - Pointer to MemoryDescriptor structure containing allocation state

Returns:
Slot index (0-31) on successful allocation
-1 on VirtualAlloc failure

Special Cases:

0x144 (324) - Base descriptor offset 
0x8000 (32768) - Memory block size (32KB)
0x1000 (4096) - VirtualAlloc MEM_COMMIT flag
0x3f (63) - Loop counter for 64 node pairs
0x400 (1024) - Node stride in memory block
0xff0 (4080) - Node size/offset marker
0x1c00 (7168) - Memory block boundary check

functions.name: ProcessHeapFreeBlock
functions.signature: bool ProcessHeapFreeBlock(MemoryAllocation * pAllocator, uint dwBlockPtr, uint dwRequestedSize)
functions.comment:
Processes a heap memory block for allocation by splitting oversized blocks and updating free list structures.

Algorithm:
1. Align requested size to 16-byte boundaries with header overhead (size + 0x17) & 0xfffffff0
2. Calculate chunk index by shifting block address difference by 15 bits for 32KB regions
3. Compute free list base address using chunk index * 0x204 + 0x144 + allocator state
4. Read current block size from header at [block - 4] and block metadata from [block - 5]
5. Validate block is not in use (bit 0 clear) and has sufficient size for request
6. If current block size < aligned request: return false (insufficient space)
7. If exact size match: mark block allocated and return true
8. If oversized block: split into allocated portion and remainder
9. Calculate size class index from block size (size >> 4) - 1, capped at 63 (0x3f)
10. For blocks being removed from free list: update size class reference counters
11. Clear size class bitmap bits when reference counter reaches zero
12. For new remainder blocks: link into appropriate size class free list
13. Set size class bitmap bits when first block added to empty list
14. Update block headers with new sizes and allocation status flags

Parameters:
pAllocator - Pointer to MemoryAllocation structure containing allocator state and bitmaps
nBlockPtr - Memory address of block to process for allocation
nRequestedSize - Size in bytes requested by caller (will be aligned internally)

Returns:
true (1) - Block successfully processed and allocated
false (0) - Block cannot satisfy request (insufficient size or validation failed)

Special Cases:
Size class bitmap management uses dual bitmap arrays for 64 size classes:
- Classes 0-31: Primary bitmap at pAllocator[0], counters at [state + 4], chunk bitmaps at [state + 0x44]
- Classes 32-63: Secondary bitmap at pAllocator[1], counters at [state + 4], chunk bitmaps at [state + 0xc4]

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x17 (23 dec) - Block header overhead for 16-byte alignment calculation
0xfffffff0 - Alignment mask for 16-byte boundaries
0xf (15 dec) - Right shift amount for 32KB chunk size calculation
0x204 (516 dec) - Size of free list structure per chunk
0x144 (324 dec) - Base offset to free list array in allocator state
0x3f (63 dec) - Maximum size class index (supports 64 total size classes)
0x20 (32 dec) - Threshold between primary and secondary bitmap arrays
0x44 (68 dec) - Offset to primary chunk bitmap array in allocator state
0xc4 (196 dec) - Offset to secondary chunk bitmap array in allocator state
0x80000000 - Bit mask constant for bitmap manipulation operations

Structure Layout:
Block Header Format (at block - 4):
Offset  Size  Field Name      Type    Description
+0      4     nBlockSize      uint    Total block size including headers
-4      4     nPrevBlockSize  uint    Size of previous block (for coalescing)

Free List Node Format (for unallocated blocks):
Offset  Size  Field Name   Type    Description  
+4      4     pNext        void*   Next block in free list
+8      4     pPrev        void*   Previous block in free list

functions.name: FormatStringProcessor
functions.signature: int FormatStringProcessor(int * pOutputHandler, byte * pbFormatString, uint * ppnArgsPtr)
functions.comment:
FormatStringProcessor - processes printf-style format strings with variable arguments

Algorithm:
1. Initialize state variables: dwFlags=0, nStateIndex=0, nCharCount=0
2. Begin character-by-character processing loop of format string
3. For each character, determine processing state using lookup table at 0x6ff333e0
4. Execute state machine transitions based on current state (0-7):
   - State 0: Output literal characters, handle character attributes
   - State 1: Initialize format specifier parsing, reset all flags
   - State 2: Parse format flags: space(0x02), hash(0x80), plus(0x01), minus(0x04), zero(0x08)
   - State 3: Parse field width (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)
   - State 4: Encountered decimal point, prepare for precision parsing
   - State 5: Parse precision (decimal digits or asterisk for va_arg)  
   - State 6: Parse length modifiers: I64(0x8000), h(0x20), l(0x10), w(0x800)
   - State 7: Process conversion specifiers and generate output
5. For conversion specifiers: handle integer(d,i,u,o,x,X), float(e,E,f,g,G), character(c,C), string(s,S), pointer(p), written count(n)
6. Apply formatting: field width padding, precision truncation, sign prefixes, case conversion
7. Convert wide characters to multibyte when needed using FUN_6ff30505
8. Output formatted result through pOutputHandler callback
9. Continue until null terminator reached
10. Return total character count

Parameters:
  pOutputHandler (int *) - callback function pointer for character output
  pbFormatString (byte *) - printf-style format string to process
  ppnArgsPtr (uint *) - pointer to variable arguments list array

Returns:
  int - total number of characters processed and output, or negative on error

Special Cases:
  - Field width of -1 indicates unlimited width (0x7fffffff)
  - Precision of -1 disables precision limiting
  - Zero flag (0x08) is ignored when left-align flag (0x04) is set
  - Hash flag (0x80) adds prefixes: "0" for octal, "0x"/"0X" for hex
  - I64 modifier (0x8000) enables 64-bit integer processing

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x6ff333e0 - character classification table for format parsing
  0x6ff33400 - state transition table (8 bytes per character class)  
  0x20/0x78 - valid format character range (space to 'x')
  0x7fffffff - unlimited field width sentinel value
  0x30 - ASCII '0', base for digit conversion
  0x39 - ASCII '9', upper limit for digit checking
  0x2a - ASCII '*', indicates va_arg width/precision
  0x2d - ASCII '-', negative sign character

Error Handling:
  - Invalid format characters fall through to literal output
  - Null string arguments replaced with default "(null)" string
  - Negative field widths converted to left-align with positive width
  - Buffer overflow protection through character count tracking

functions.name: BufferedPutChar
functions.signature: int BufferedPutChar(byte bCharacter, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
functions.comment:
Writes a single character to a buffered output stream with automatic flushing.

Algorithm:
1. Decrement the buffer's remaining byte count
2. If buffer has space (count >= 0):
   a. Store character at current buffer position
   b. Increment buffer pointer
   c. Return character value (masked to 8 bits)
3. If buffer is full (count < 0):
   a. Call flush/refill function FUN_6ff2d034
   b. Use its return value as result
4. Check for error condition (-1 return value):
   a. If error: set chars written counter to -1
   b. If success: increment chars written counter

Parameters:
chCharacter (byte) - Character to write to buffer (0-255)
pBuffer (FileBuffer *) - Pointer to buffer structure containing:
  - pbCurrent: Current write position in buffer
  - dwBytesRemaining: Number of bytes left in buffer
pnCharsWritten (int *) - Pointer to character count/status tracker

Returns:
Character value (0-255) on success
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF) on error or buffer flush failure

Special Cases:
If buffer flush operation fails, error state is propagated to caller
Characters are masked to 8 bits (param_1 & 0xff) for return value
Negative buffer count triggers automatic flush/refill operation

Magic Numbers Reference:
0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Error indicator for failed operations

Structure Layout:
FileBuffer (8 bytes):
Offset  Size  Field Name         Type    Description
0x00    4     pbCurrent          byte*   Current write position
0x04    4     dwBytesRemaining   uint    Bytes remaining in buffer

functions.name: RepeatCharacterToStream
functions.signature: void RepeatCharacterToStream(uint dwCharacter, int nCount, int * pOutputStream, int * pnErrorStatus)
functions.comment:
Writes a specified character to an output stream a given number of times.

Algorithm:
1. Check if repeat count is positive, return immediately if zero or negative
2. Enter loop to repeat character output nCount times
3. Call FUN_6ff2d88d to write dwCharacter to pOutputStream 
4. Check error status after each write operation
5. If *pnErrorStatus equals -1, terminate early with error
6. Decrement count and continue loop if count > 0
7. Exit when all characters written or error encountered

Parameters:
dwCharacter (uint): Character code to repeat (typically ASCII value 0x20 for space, 0x30 for '0')
nCount (int): Number of times to repeat the character 
pOutputStream (int *): Pointer to output stream buffer structure
pnErrorStatus (int *): Pointer to error status flag, set to -1 on write failure

Returns:
void: No return value, error status communicated through pnErrorStatus

Special Cases:
- If nCount <= 0, function returns immediately without writing
- Loop terminates early if write operation sets *pnErrorStatus to -1
- Used for padding in printf formatting (spaces, zeros)

Error Handling:
- Monitors error status after each character write
- Early termination on first write failure (-1 status)
- Calling function must check pnErrorStatus for final status

functions.name: WriteStringToBuffer
functions.signature: void WriteStringToBuffer(char * lpszString, int nLength, FileBuffer * pBuffer, int * pnCharsWritten)
functions.comment:
Writes a string to a buffered output stream character by character with error checking.

Algorithm:
1. Validate that string length is greater than zero
2. Initialize loop variables and counters  
3. For each character in the string:
   a. Decrement remaining character count
   b. Load current character from string pointer
   c. Advance string pointer to next character
   d. Call BufferedPutChar to write character to buffer
   e. Check if write operation failed (error code -1)
   f. If error occurred, exit immediately
   g. If characters remain, continue to next character
4. Return when all characters processed or error encountered

Parameters:
lpszString (char *): Pointer to null-terminated or fixed-length string to write
nLength (int): Number of characters to write from string
pBuffer (FileBuffer *): Pointer to buffered output stream structure
pnCharsWritten (int *): Pointer to counter tracking total characters written

Returns:
void - No return value; error status communicated through pnCharsWritten pointer

Special Cases:
If nLength <= 0, function returns immediately without processing
If BufferedPutChar fails (sets *pnCharsWritten to -1), loop exits early
String pointer is advanced byte-by-byte regardless of character encoding

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x1: Byte increment for string pointer advancement (0x6ff2d90d: INC ESI)
-1 (0xFFFFFFFF): Error status code indicating write failure (0x6ff2d91b: CMP dword ptr [EDI],-0x1)

functions.name: ReadAndAdvancePointer
functions.comment:
Reads a 32-bit value from current pointer position and advances the pointer by one element.

3. Return the value that was at the original position before advancement

Parameters:

The 32-bit unsigned integer value that was at the current position before advancement

and parsing operations. The caller maintains a cursor pointer that gets automatically
advanced after each read operation.

Algorithm:

2. Advance the pointer by 8 bytes (2 * sizeof(uint)) to skip over the 8-byte value
3. Read and return the 8-byte value from the original position before advancement

Parameters:

Returns:

  - Reads value from position before advancement (offset -8 from new position)

2. Read 16-bit value from previous argument position (offset -4)

Parameters:

Returns:

functions.name: ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp
functions.signature: int ConvertDateTimeToTimestamp(int nYear, int nMonth, int nDay, int nHour, int nMinute, int nSecond, int nDaylightSavingFlag)
functions.comment:
Converts date and time components to a Unix-style timestamp value.

Algorithm:
1. Validate year is in supported range (1900-1994, offset from 0x76c base)
2. Return -1 if year is outside valid range [0x46, 0x8a] from base
3. Calculate cumulative days from month table at g_adDaysInMonths[nMonth]
4. Add specified day to cumulative month days
5. Apply leap year adjustment: if year divisible by 4 and month > 2, add 1 day
6. Call FUN_6ff306b5() to update internal state
7. Calculate total timestamp: ((nHour + (yearOffset * 365 + daysFromMonth + (year-1)/4) * 24) * 60 + nMinute) * 60 + baseOffset + second
8. Apply timezone adjustment if nDaylightSavingFlag == 1 or timezone check passes
9. Return final timestamp value

Parameters:
nYear - Year value (1900-1994 supported range)
nMonth - Month index (0-11, used to index days table)
nDay - Day of month (1-31)
nHour - Hour component (0-23)
nMinute - Minute component (0-59) 
nSecond - Second component (0-59)
nDaylightSavingFlag - DST flag: 1=apply DST, -1=check timezone, 0=standard time

Returns:
Calculated timestamp as signed integer
-1 if year is outside supported range

Special Cases:
Leap year handling: Years divisible by 4 get +1 day if month > February
Timezone adjustment: Applied based on g_dwTimezoneFlag and DST settings
Base offset: 0x7c558180 provides epoch adjustment

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x76c (1900) - Base year offset for calculations
0x46 (70) - Minimum year offset (1970)
0x8a (138) - Maximum year offset (2038)
0x16d (365) - Days per year for calculation
0x18 (24) - Hours per day
0x3c (60) - Minutes per hour, seconds per minute
0x7c558180 - Unix epoch base offset

    0 (false) if floating point modulus is greater than or equal to pi constant

functions.name: ProcessLocaleStringTransform

Processes locale-specific string transformation with character skipping and rotation.

Algorithm:

2. If converted character equals 'e' (0x65), skip to character rotation step  
3. Otherwise, enter character skipping loop

7. For function call mode: Call FUN_1001fbc2 with character value and constant 4
8. Continue until character test returns 0 (non-whitespace character found)
9. Perform character rotation at end of string
10. Save current character and replace with global DAT_1002e918
11. Iterate through remaining string, shifting characters one position
12. Continue until null terminator reached

Parameters:
pLocaleContext - Locale context object containing character mapping data and locale settings
lpszString - Input string to process and transform in-place

Returns:
void - Function modifies string in-place, no return value

Special Cases:
If first character converts to 'e' (0x65), skips whitespace removal entirely
String rotation uses global character value DAT_1002e918 as insertion point
Function handles two different locale modes based on DAT_1002e914 threshold
Character lookup table uses stride of 2 bytes per character entry

0x4 - Bitmask for character classification in lookup table  
0x2 - Stride multiplier for lookup table access (PTR_DAT_1002e708[char * 2])
DAT_1002e914 - Locale mode selector (< 2 = table, >= 2 = function)

functions.name: GlobalUnwind2
functions.comment:
Performs global stack unwinding to a specified frame using Windows RtlUnwind API.

Algorithm:
1. Validate input parameter (target frame pointer)
2. Save all non-volatile registers (EBX, ESI, EDI, EBP) to preserve caller state
3. Prepare RtlUnwind parameters:
   - TargetFrame: Caller-specified frame to unwind to
   - TargetIp: Fixed continuation address (0x1001cdf0) for post-unwind execution
   - ExceptionRecord: NULL (no exception context)
   - ReturnValue: NULL (no specific return value)
4. Call Windows RtlUnwind API to perform structured exception unwinding
5. Restore all saved registers maintaining calling convention
6. Return to caller with stack properly unwound

Parameters:
pTargetFrame (void*): Target stack frame pointer to unwind to. Must be valid frame 
                     pointer from current call chain. NULL terminates unwinding at 
                     top-level exception handler.

Returns:
void: Function does not return value. Unwind operation modifies stack state and 
      control flow continues at TargetIp (0x1001cdf0) after unwinding completes.

Special Cases:
- Magic Number 0x1001cdf0: Hardcoded continuation address where execution resumes 
  after unwinding. Points to register restoration sequence (POP EBP instruction).
- NULL pTargetFrame: Unwinds entire stack to process termination handler
- Invalid frame pointer: RtlUnwind handles validation and may terminate process

Error Handling:
RtlUnwind handles all error conditions including invalid frame pointers, corrupted 
stack, and access violations. Function acts as thin wrapper without additional 
validation or error recovery.

functions.name: LocalUnwindTwo
functions.comment:
Performs structured exception handling (SEH) local unwinding to a target level.

Algorithm:
1. Setup exception registration frame with current exception list
2. Enter loop to process each unwind level from current to target
3. Load unwind table pointer from SEH frame at offset +8
4. Load current level from SEH frame at offset +12  
5. Check termination conditions: level -1 (end) or target level reached
6. Calculate unwind record index using current level * 12 bytes
7. Load previous level from unwind table entry at offset +0
8. Update SEH frame current level to previous level
9. Check exception filter flag at unwind table offset +4
10. If filter flag is 0, call exception filter function and cleanup handler
11. Continue loop until target level or end reached
12. Restore previous exception list and return

Parameters:
pSehFrame (SehFrame *): Pointer to SEH frame containing unwind table and current level
nTargetLevel (int): Target unwind level to stop unwinding at (-1 means unwind all)

Returns:
void: No return value, modifies SEH frame state directly

Special Cases:
- If current level is -1, unwinding is already complete
- If target level equals current level, no unwinding needed  
- Filter flag 0x00000000 indicates active exception handler that needs cleanup

Structure Layout:
SehFrame (16 bytes):
Offset Size Field Name      Type              Description
0x00   4    pExceptionRecord void*            Pointer to exception record
0x04   4    dwCurrentLevel   uint             Current exception nesting level  
0x08   4    pUnwindTable     SehUnwindRecord* Pointer to unwind table array
0x0C   4    dwTryLevel       uint             Current try block level

SehUnwindRecord (12 bytes):
Offset Size Field Name      Type              Description  
0x00   4    dwPrevLevel     uint             Previous exception level in chain
0x04   4    dwFlags         uint             Exception filter flags (0=active)
0x08   4    pfnHandler      void*            Exception handler function pointer

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x08 (8): Offset to unwind table pointer in SEH frame
0x0C (12): Offset to current level in SEH frame, also stride of unwind records
0x04 (4): Offset to flags field in unwind record
0x08 (8): Offset to handler function in unwind record
0xFFFFFFFF (-1): End-of-chain marker for exception levels

2. Check if divisor high word is zero (simple 64/32 division case)
3. Simple case: Use 32-bit division operations to compute quotient directly
4. Complex case: Normalize both operands by shifting right until divisor fits in 32 bits
5. Perform approximate division using normalized 32-bit values
6. Multiply trial quotient by original divisor to get product

  Overflow: Cannot occur with unsigned division

  - Uses binary long division when divisor > 32 bits
  - Normalizes operands to avoid overflow during intermediate calculations
  - Trial-and-error approach with correction ensures accuracy
  - Optimized for common case where divisor fits in 32 bits

2. If divisor fits in 32 bits, perform standard division on combined 64-bit dividend
3. Otherwise, normalize operands by right-shifting until divisor fits in 32 bits
4. Perform division on normalized values to get approximate quotient
5. Calculate full product of quotient and original divisor
6. Compare product with original dividend and adjust quotient if needed
7. Subtract final quotient×divisor from dividend to get remainder
8. Return 64-bit remainder as combined high/low 32-bit values

4. Compare timezone offset against standard values (DAT_6ff38ed8, DAT_6ff38ee8)

   - Otherwise, call complex transition functions using configuration data arrays
6. Extract year value from time info structure [offset 0x1c]
7. Check if year falls within DST date range (DAT_6ff38edc to DAT_6ff38eec)
8. If year is within range bounds, return true for dates between boundaries
9. If year equals boundary values, perform detailed time-of-day comparison:
   - Calculate total milliseconds: ((hours * 60 + minutes) * 60 + seconds) * 1000
   - For start boundary (DAT_6ff38edc), check if time >= start threshold (DAT_6ff38ee0)
   - For end boundary (DAT_6ff38eec), check if time < end threshold (DAT_6ff38ef0)

Parameters:
- pTimeInfo: Pointer to time/date structure containing:
  [0x0] seconds (0-59)
  [0x4] minutes (0-59) 
  [0x8] hours (0-23)
  [0x14] timezone offset value
  [0x1c] year value

Returns:
- true: Date/time falls within daylight saving transition period
- false: Date/time is outside DST transition period or timezone processing disabled

Special Cases:
- Returns false immediately if g_dwTimezoneFlag is 0
- Handles wrap-around year ranges when start year > end year
- Precise millisecond comparison at DST boundary dates

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x3c (60): Seconds per minute, minutes per hour conversion
- 0x3e8 (1000): Milliseconds per second conversion
- 0x14 (20): Offset to timezone field in time structure
- 0x1c (28): Offset to year field in time structure

functions.name: CalculateAndSetCalendarDateTime
functions.signature: void CalculateAndSetCalendarDateTime(int nMode, int nCalculationMode, uint dwYear, int nMonth, int nWeek, int nDayOfWeek, int nDayOffset, int nHour, int nMinute, int nSecond, int nMillisecond)
functions.comment:
Calculates calendar day numbers and time values, setting global date/time state variables.

Algorithm:
1. Check calculation mode (nCalculationMode) to determine calendar vs simple calculation 
2. For calendar mode (nCalculationMode == 1):
   a. Determine if year is leap year using bitwise test (dwYear & 3 == 0)
   b. Get days in month from appropriate array (leap year vs normal year)
   c. Calculate day of week using formula: (dwYear * 0x16d - 0x63db + dwDaysInMonth + 1 + ((dwYear-1) >> 2)) % 7
   d. Adjust calculated day based on week number (nWeek) and target day of week (nDayOfWeek)
   e. Handle week 5 special case - if calculated day exceeds month length, subtract 7
3. For simple mode (nCalculationMode != 1):
   a. Get days in target month using same leap year logic
   b. Add day offset (nDayOffset) directly to month days
4. Convert time components to milliseconds: ((nHour * 60 + nMinute) * 60 + nSecond) * 1000 + nMillisecond  
5. Check mode flag (nMode) to determine global variable assignment:
   a. Mode 1: Store values in g_dwStoredYear, g_dwStoredMilliseconds, g_nStoredDay
   b. Mode 0: Apply daylight adjustment and handle day rollover, store in g_dwAdjustedYear, g_dwAdjustedTimeMilliseconds, g_nAdjustedDay

Parameters:
nMode - Mode flag determining which global variables to update (1=stored, 0=adjusted)
nCalculationMode - Calculation type flag (1=calendar calculation, other=simple day offset)
dwYear - Year for calendar calculations and leap year determination  
nMonth - Zero-based month index for array lookups (0=January, 11=December)
nWeek - Week number within month (0-4, where 4 is special case for month end)
nDayOfWeek - Target day of week for calendar calculations (0-6)
nDayOffset - Simple day offset added to month days in non-calendar mode
nHour - Hour component (0-23) for time calculation
nMinute - Minute component (0-59) for time calculation  
nSecond - Second component (0-59) for time calculation
nMillisecond - Millisecond component (0-999) for time calculation

Returns:
void - Function updates global state variables rather than returning values

Special Cases:
Week 5 handling: If nWeek == 5 and calculated day exceeds month length, subtract 7 days
Day rollover: In mode 0, if time with daylight adjustment goes negative or exceeds 86,399,999ms, adjust day accordingly
Leap year detection: Uses bitwise AND with 3 (dwYear & 3 == 0) for simple leap year test

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x16d (365) - Days per year for day-of-week calculation
0x63db (25,563) - Calendar epoch adjustment constant  
0x3e8 (1,000) - Milliseconds per second conversion
0x3c (60) - Seconds per minute / minutes per hour conversion
0x5265c00 (86,400,000) - Milliseconds per day (24 * 60 * 60 * 1000)
0x5265c01 (86,400,001) - Day overflow threshold (one millisecond past midnight)

functions.name: UpdateFpuControlBits
functions.signature: uint UpdateFpuControlBits(void * this, uint param_1, uint param_2)
functions.comment:
Modifies specific bits in the floating point unit control word register.

Algorithm:
1. Save current FPU control word to stack using FSTCW instruction
2. Combine saved control word with upper 16 bits of context pointer into composite value
3. Retrieve current FPU control word value via GetFpuControlWord()
4. Apply bit mask operation: (current & ~dwBitMask) | (dwNewBits & dwBitMask)
5. Set updated FPU control word via SetFpuControlWord()
6. Restore original FPU control word from stack using FLDCW instruction
7. Return the updated control word value

Parameters:
- this (void*): Context pointer (upper 16 bits used in composite value)
- dwNewBits (uint): New bit values to apply where mask is set
- dwBitMask (uint): Bit mask indicating which bits to modify (1=modify, 0=preserve)

Returns:
- uint: Updated FPU control word value after applying bit modifications

Special Cases:
- If dwBitMask is 0x0000, function returns current control word unchanged
- If dwBitMask is 0xFFFF, function returns dwNewBits (full replacement)
- IMPLICIT: Original FPU control word is preserved and restored

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x10: Bit shift for extracting upper 16 bits of context pointer
- FSTCW: Store FPU Control Word (saves current state)
- FLDCW: Load FPU Control Word (restores saved state)

Error Handling:
- Function assumes valid context pointer and control word operations
- No validation of bit mask or new bit values
- FPU control word operations are atomic at instruction level

functions.name: GetFpuControlWord
functions.comment:
Convert FPU control flags from one format to another for FPU control register updates.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize target flags to 0
2. Test source flag bit 0 (0x01) - if set, OR target with 0x10 (exception enable bit 4)
3. Test source flag bit 2 (0x04) - if set, OR target with 0x08 (exception enable bit 3) 
4. Test source flag bit 3 (0x08) - if set, OR target with 0x04 (exception enable bit 2)
5. Test source flag bit 4 (0x10) - if set, OR target with 0x02 (exception enable bit 1)
6. Test source flag bit 5 (0x20) - if set, OR target with 0x01 (exception enable bit 0)
7. Test source flag bit 1 (0x02) - if set, OR target with 0x80000 (special control bit)
8. Extract precision control bits (bits 10-11, mask 0xc00) from source
9. Map precision control: 0x400->0x100, 0x800->0x200, 0xc00->0x300
10. Extract rounding control bits (bits 8-9, mask 0x300) from source
11. Map rounding control: 0x00->0x20000, 0x200->0x10000, others->no change
12. Test source flag bit 12 (0x1000) - if set, OR target with 0x40000
13. Return converted target flags

Parameters:
dwSourceFlags - Input FPU control flags in source format to be converted

Returns:
Converted FPU control flags in target format for hardware register update

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x01 - Source exception enable bit 0 -> Target bit 4 (0x10)
0x02 - Source special control bit -> Target bit 19 (0x80000)
0x04 - Source exception enable bit 2 -> Target bit 3 (0x08)
0x08 - Source exception enable bit 3 -> Target bit 2 (0x04)
0x10 - Source exception enable bit 4 -> Target bit 1 (0x02)
0x20 - Source exception enable bit 5 -> Target bit 0 (0x01)
0x300 - Rounding control mask (bits 8-9)
0xc00 - Precision control mask (bits 10-11)
0x1000 - Source control bit 12 -> Target bit 18 (0x40000)
0x10000 - Target rounding mode: round towards nearest
0x20000 - Target rounding mode: round towards zero (truncate)
0x100, 0x200, 0x300 - Target precision control values
0x40000 - Target control bit for infinity control

Flag Bits:
Source Format Bits -> Target Format Bits
Bit 0 (0x01): Exception mask 0 -> Exception enable 4 (0x10)
Bit 1 (0x02): Special control -> Control bit 19 (0x80000)  
Bit 2 (0x04): Exception mask 2 -> Exception enable 3 (0x08)
Bit 3 (0x08): Exception mask 3 -> Exception enable 2 (0x04)
Bit 4 (0x10): Exception mask 4 -> Exception enable 1 (0x02)
Bit 5 (0x20): Exception mask 5 -> Exception enable 0 (0x01)
Bits 8-9 (0x300): Rounding control -> Rounding mode (0x10000/0x20000)
Bits 10-11 (0xc00): Precision control -> Precision mode (0x100/0x200/0x300)
Bit 12 (0x1000): Infinity control -> Control bit 18 (0x40000)

functions.name: ConvertFpuControlToMxcsr
functions.comment:
Converts x87 FPU control word bit flags to SSE MXCSR control register format.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize result to 0 and extract invalid operation mask from bit 4 of FPU control word
2. Convert FPU exception mask bits to MXCSR format:
   - Bit 3 (divide-by-zero) → MXCSR bit 2 (0x04)
   - Bit 2 (denormal) → MXCSR bit 3 (0x08) 
   - Bit 1 (overflow) → MXCSR bit 4 (0x10)
   - Bit 0 (underflow) → MXCSR bit 5 (0x20)
3. Convert FPU flush-to-zero from bit 19 (0x80000) to MXCSR bit 1 (0x02)
4. Extract and convert rounding mode from bits 8-9 (0x300):
   - 0x100 (round to nearest) → MXCSR bits 10-11 (0x400)
   - 0x200 (round down) → MXCSR bit 11 (0x800)
   - 0x300 (round up) → MXCSR bits 10-11 (0xC00)
5. Convert precision control from bits 16-17 (0x30000):
   - 0x00000 (24-bit) → MXCSR bits 8-9 (0x300)
   - 0x10000 (53-bit) → MXCSR bit 9 (0x200)
   - 0x20000 (64-bit) → No MXCSR equivalent (default)
6. Convert infinity control from bit 18 (0x40000) to MXCSR bit 12 (0x1000)

Parameters:
  dwFpuControlWord - x87 FPU control word containing exception masks, rounding mode, precision control

Returns:
  Equivalent MXCSR control register value with converted bit flags

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x10 (16) - FPU invalid operation mask bit
  0x08 (8) - FPU divide-by-zero mask bit  
  0x04 (4) - FPU denormal operand mask bit
  0x02 (2) - FPU overflow mask bit
  0x01 (1) - FPU underflow mask bit
  0x80000 (524288) - FPU flush-to-zero flag
  0x300 (768) - FPU rounding mode mask (bits 8-9)
  0x100 (256) - Round to nearest even
  0x200 (512) - Round toward negative infinity
  0x300 (768) - Round toward positive infinity
  0x30000 (196608) - FPU precision control mask (bits 16-17)
  0x10000 (65536) - 53-bit precision (double)
  0x40000 (262144) - FPU infinity control bit
  0x400 (1024) - MXCSR round to nearest (bits 13-14)
  0x800 (2048) - MXCSR round down (bit 14)
  0xC00 (3072) - MXCSR round up (bits 13-14)
  0x1000 (4096) - MXCSR denormals-are-zero flag

functions.name: CheckBitfieldSlotAvailable
functions.comment:
Checks if a bit position in a 32-bit DWORD array is available (clear) and all subsequent DWORDs are also clear.

Algorithm:

1. Calculate target DWORD index by dividing bit index by 32 (0x20)
2. Calculate bit position within DWORD using modulo operation
3. Create bit mask using left shift and bitwise NOT to test target bit
4. Test if target bit is set - if so, position is unavailable, return false
5. Calculate starting array index (DWORD index + 1) for subsequent checks
6. If starting index is less than 3, iterate through remaining array elements
7. Check each DWORD from starting index to index 2 (3 total DWORDs maximum)
8. If any DWORD contains non-zero value, position is unavailable, return false
9. If all checks pass, position is available, return true

Parameters:
- pdwBitfield: Pointer to DWORD array used as bitfield (minimum 3 DWORDs, 12 bytes)
- nBitIndex: Zero-based bit position to check (0-95 for 3 DWORD array)

Returns:
- true (1): Bit position is clear and all subsequent DWORDs are zero
- false (0): Bit position is set OR subsequent DWORDs contain non-zero values

Special Cases:
- If bit index results in DWORD index 2 or higher, no subsequent DWORD checking needed
- Function assumes array has at least 3 DWORDs (indices 0, 1, 2)
- Uses 32-bit arithmetic for bit calculations (0x20 = 32, 0x1f = 31)

Magic Numbers Reference:
- 0x20 (32): Bits per DWORD for index calculation
- 0x1f (31): Maximum bit position within DWORD (bit mask)
- 0x1fU (31): Unsigned constant for bit position calculation
- 3: Maximum array index checked (indices 0, 1, 2)
- 4: Byte increment for DWORD pointer arithmetic

functions.name: ClearBitArrayRange
functions.comment:
Process bitmap bits from specified offset through end of buffer

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word index (nBitOffset / 32) and bit offset within word (nBitOffset % 32)
2. Create bit mask for starting position: 1 << (31 - bit_offset)
3. Call ProcessBitOperation on first word with calculated mask
4. If operation returns 0, exit (typically indicates completion)
5. Decrement word index
6. Loop through remaining words from current to word 0 with mask=1
7. Each iteration: call ProcessBitOperation, check result, decrement index
8. Exit when all words processed or operation returns 0

Parameters:
  pBitmapBase (dword *) - Base pointer to 32-bit word array containing bitmap
  nBitOffset (int) - Starting bit offset into bitmap

Returns:
  void - Operation result indicated by side effects in buffer

Special Cases:
  - If nBitOffset >= total bits in buffer, behavior depends on loop guard
  - First word uses masked operation, subsequent words use mask=1
  - Early exit when operation returns non-zero value
  - Note: EDI register used as pBitmapWord pointer throughout function

Magic Numbers:
  0x20 (32) - Bits per word for division to get word index
  0x1f (31) - Bit position for creating shift mask
  1 - Mask value for complete word in loop

Structure Layout:
Bitmap is an array of 32-bit words where each bit position represents a flag or state:
  Offset | Size | Meaning
  -------|------|--------
  +0     |  4   | Word N (32 bits)

functions.name: ClearBitAndTruncateHigh
functions.comment:
Clears a bit at the specified index and truncates all higher bits in a 96-bit bitfield.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word index by dividing bit index by 0x20 (32)
2. Calculate bit position within word using modulo 0x20
3. Get pointer to the target 32-bit word in the bitfield
4. Calculate bit shift value as (0x1F - bit_position)
5. Check if the target bit is currently set using bit mask
6. If bit is set and no higher bits are set (via CheckBitfieldSlotAvailable), call FUN_1001fde6 with previous index
7. Clear the target bit using AND with inverted bit mask
8. Calculate starting word for high-bit clearing (word_index + 1)
9. If more words exist (word_index < 2), clear all remaining high words
10. Return the value from step 6 or 0 if bit was not set

Parameters:
pBitfield - Pointer to 96-bit bitfield (3 x 32-bit words, 12 bytes total)
nBitIndex - Zero-based bit position to clear (0-95 range)

Returns:
Integer value from FUN_1001fde6 if bit was set and no higher bits exist, 0 otherwise

Special Cases:
Bitfield is exactly 96 bits (3 x 32-bit words)
Bit index 0x20 (32) targets second word, 0x40 (64) targets third word
Higher bit clearing always clears from next word boundary to end

Magic Numbers Reference:
0x20 (32) - Bits per word, used for word boundary calculations
0x1F (31) - Bit mask for position within word
0x3 (3) - Total number of 32-bit words in 96-bit bitfield

Error Handling:
No bounds checking on bit index - caller must ensure 0 <= nBitIndex <= 95
No null pointer validation on pBitfield parameter

Offset | Size | Field Name    | Type | Description
0x00   | 4    | dwLowBits     | uint | Bits 0-31
0x04   | 4    | dwMidBits     | uint | Bits 32-63  
0x08   | 4    | dwHighBits    | uint | Bits 64-95

functions.name: CopyThreeIntegers
functions.comment:
Copies three consecutive 32-bit integers from source to destination using offset-based addressing.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate offset between destination address and source pointer address
2. Initialize counter to 3 for three integer copy operations
3. Enter copy loop:
   a. Read current source integer value
   b. Store value at destination using calculated offset + current source position
   c. Advance source pointer by 4 bytes (one integer)
   d. Decrement counter
   e. Continue while counter > 0
4. Return when all three integers copied

Parameters:
- nDestination (int): Target memory address where integers will be copied
- pSource (uint *): Source pointer to array of 32-bit unsigned integers

Returns:
- void: No return value, performs in-place memory copy operation

Special Cases:

- Uses pointer arithmetic with offset calculation for addressing
- No bounds checking or validation performed

Magic Numbers Reference:

- 0x4 (4): Size increment per iteration (sizeof(uint))
- 0x1 (1): Decrement value for loop counter

functions.name: ZeroFloatComponents

2. Clear EAX register to zero
3. Store zero to first component [EDI] and increment EDI by 4
4. Store zero to second component [EDI+4] and increment EDI by 4  
5. Store zero to third component [EDI+8] and increment EDI by 4
6. Restore EDI register and return

Parameters:

Checks whether the first three integers in an array are all zero.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize loop counter (nIndex) to 0
2. Enter do-while loop for three iterations
3. Check if current array element is non-zero
4. If non-zero found, return 0 (false) immediately
5. Increment loop counter and advance array pointer by 4 bytes
6. Continue loop while counter < 3
7. If all three elements are zero, return 1 (true)

Parameters:
  pnArray - int * - Pointer to integer array to check (must have at least 3 elements)

Returns:
  1 - All first three elements are zero (validation passed)
  0 - At least one of the first three elements is non-zero (validation failed)

Special Cases:
  Function assumes pnArray points to valid memory with at least 3 integers
  No null pointer validation performed - caller must ensure valid array

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x3 (3) - Number of array elements to check
  0x4 (4) - Size of int in bytes for pointer arithmetic

functions.name: ShiftBigIntegerRight
functions.comment:
Performs right bit shift operation on 128-bit integer stored as 4-element uint32 array.

Algorithm:
1. Calculate word shifts (dwShiftCount / 0x20) and bit shifts (dwShiftCount % 0x20)
2. Initialize carry accumulator (param_2 = 0) and bit shift amount (byBitShifts)
3. For each of 4 array elements (index 0-3):
   a. Load current element value (dwCurrentElement)
   b. Shift element right by bit amount, OR with previous carry
   c. Calculate new carry from bits being shifted out
   d. Store shifted result back to array element
   e. Advance to next element pointer
4. Handle additional word-level shifts for elements 2 down to 0:
   a. If source index < word shifts: clear destination element (set to 0)
   b. Otherwise: copy element from shifted source position
   c. Decrement both source index and destination offset by 4 bytes

Parameters:
  pBigInteger: Pointer to 4-element uint32 array representing 128-bit integer
  dwShiftCount: Number of bits to shift right (0-127 valid range)

Returns:
  void - Operation modifies array in-place

Special Cases:
  - Shift count 0: No operation performed, array unchanged
  - Shift count >= 32: Combines bit shifts with word-level element movement
  - Shift count >= 128: All elements become 0 (complete right shift out)

Magic Numbers:
  0x20 (32): Bits per 32-bit word, used for word/bit shift separation
  0x1f (31): Bit mask for shift amount (ensures valid 0-31 bit shifts)
  0x3: Initial element counter (processes 4 elements: indices 0,1,2,3)
  0x8 (8): Starting byte offset for element 2 (8 = 2 * sizeof(uint32))
  0x2: Starting element index for reverse copy (element 2)

Structure Layout:
Offset | Size | Field       | Type | Description
-------|------|-------------|------|----------------------------------
0x00   | 4    | element[0]  | uint | Least significant 32 bits
0x04   | 4    | element[1]  | uint | Second 32-bit word  
0x08   | 4    | element[2]  | uint | Third 32-bit word
0x0C   | 4    | element[3]  | uint | Most significant 32 bits
